guard_streams.source: Moving landline phones to digital technology: what you need to know
guard_streams.write_limit: Digital-landline migration guidance and resilience duties do not establish fixed-broadband availability, live orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the consumer guide on 7 February 2024.
The guide was last updated on 19 February 2026.
The public switched telephone network is old and becoming harder and more expensive to maintain.
BT plans to retire its PSTN by January 2027 and providers using that network follow the same timescale.
Future landline calls are delivered using Voice over Internet Protocol, also called digital phone or digital voice.
Customers do not need to act until their provider contacts them about the change.
A digital phone requires battery back-up to work during a power cut.
Providers should offer a free resilience solution to customers dependent on their landline for emergency calls.
The provider should arrange equipment needed to keep the main telephone connected.
Care alarms, security alarms and fax machines may need replacement or reconfiguration after migration.

guard_streams.source: Upgrading landlines to digital technology – what you need to know
guard_streams.write_limit: General migration instructions and equipment guidance do not verify broadband serviceability or performance at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published this guide on 13 December 2021.
The guide was last updated on 16 September 2024.
The PSTN equipment was developed and installed in the UK in the 1980s.
BT plans to retire the PSTN by January 2027.
Voice over Internet Protocol uses a broadband connection.
Migration is already occurring for some customers who upgrade packages or move home.
After migration, the phone generally plugs into a broadband router instead of the wall socket.
The provider should arrange a new router or broadband connection when needed.
Fire alarms, burglar alarms and telecare devices that use the phone line may be affected.
Providers must support landline-dependent customers with battery back-up or another emergency-calling solution.

guard_streams.source: Guidance: Protecting access to emergency organisations when there is a power cut at the customer’s premises
guard_streams.write_limit: Regulatory power-cut guidance concerns emergency-call continuity and cannot establish broadband coverage, orderability or measured parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the consultation page on 24 May 2018.
The consultation closed on 5 July 2018.
Final guidance was published on 10 October 2018.
General Condition A3 requires necessary measures for uninterrupted access to emergency organisations.
The guidance addresses migration from traditional landlines to voice services over broadband.
The underlying regulatory requirements were not changed by the guidance.
The guidance is not intended to be a definitive compliance manual.
It sets expectations for measures allowing emergency calls during a premises power cut.
The guidance is structured around four principles for providers.
Ofcom considers providers' regard to the four principles in the circumstances of each case.

guard_streams.source: Compliance monitoring programme into access to emergency services during power outages
guard_streams.write_limit: A closed compliance-monitoring programme about emergency access does not prove selected-parcel broadband availability or speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the compliance programme on 11 July 2022.
The page was last updated on 20 July 2023.
The compliance programme is closed.
The case opened on 11 July 2022.
The case closed on 20 July 2023.
Its scope was access to emergency services during power outages.
The programme considered consumer protection during migration to VoIP.
The relevant legal provision was General Condition A3.2(b).
Ofcom obtained information from more than 30 communications providers.
The sample included network providers and broadband and VoIP providers.

guard_streams.source: A summary of Ofcom's rules for phone and broadband providers
guard_streams.write_limit: A regulatory summary and voluntary-scheme index do not verify physical network availability or measured performance for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the provider-rules summary on 19 July 2023.
The page was last updated on 25 April 2025.
It covers important telecoms regulations, guidance and voluntary schemes.
The page summarises main regulations applying to phone and broadband providers.
It points providers to more detailed information.
It does not constitute legal or compliance advice from Ofcom.
The page does not include every requirement that may apply.
Each provider remains responsible for complying with all applicable obligations.
Electronic communications providers must comply with applicable General Conditions to operate UK services.
The summary records switching rules including the One Touch Switch process for residential broadband and landline customers.
